edges.description: Reduced A20 protein means reduced deubiquitinase activity at the NF-kappa-B signalling nodes A20 normally acts on.
Without adequate termination, canonical NF-kappa-B signalling persists.
Unterminated NF-kappa-B drives the proinflammatory transcriptional programme that produces the clinical disease.
A20 also restrains the NLRP3 inflammasome, a second arm shown in mouse myeloid cells. Whether it contributes in human A20 haploinsufficiency is not established in these sources.
If operative in humans, inflammasome derepression would add IL-1 driven inflammation to the NF-kappa-B arm.
Recurrent painful oral ulceration during flares, the commonest manifestation.
Recurrent genital ulceration, occurring with the oral ulcers and together forming the Behcet-like picture.
Fever attacks lasting three to seven days, and one of the features that separates this from Behcet disease.
Skin involvement, which is heterogeneous and includes pustular rash, folliculitis, vasculitic purpura and lupus-like macular rashes.
Gastrointestinal disease ranging from dull pain to severe inflammation with risk of perforation.
Relapsing and remitting nonerosive inflammatory polyarthritis with synovitis.
Demonstrates that losing A20 derepresses the NLRP3 inflammasome and produces spontaneous arthritis that does not require TNF receptor 1, which is the evidence for a second arm beyond NF-kappa-B.
edges.limitations: Three mismatches against the human disease, and they run in the same direction. The mouse is a complete knockout, not haploinsufficiency. It is restricted to the myeloid lineage rather than germline. And the arthritis it produces is erosive, whereas the arthritis in this disease is typically nonerosive. The model therefore supports the existence of the pathway rather than its operation in patients.

nodes.description: A conditional knockout deleting A20 in the myeloid lineage. It is the source of the inflammasome arm modelled in this entry, and it is a poor genetic match for the human disease, which is why that arm is graded HYPOTHETICAL.

evidence.reference_title: Negative regulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome by A20 protects against arthritis.
evidence.snippet: Myeloid-cell-specific deletion of the rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility gene A20/Tnfaip3 in mice (A20(myel-KO) mice) triggers a spontaneous erosive polyarthritis that resembles rheumatoid arthritis in patients.

nodes.description: Gastrointestinal involvement, from dull pain due to serositis or bowel inflammation through to severe inflammation carrying a risk of perforation.

evidence.reference_title: Haploinsufficiency of A20.
evidence.snippet: gastrointestinal disease (~40%), ranging from dull abdominal pain (due to serositis, ulcers, or bowel inflammation) to severe inflammation with risk of bowel perforation

nodes.description: Relapsing, remitting, typically nonerosive inflammatory polyarthritis with synovitis. Erosive disease resembling rheumatoid or psoriatic arthritis is rare.

evidence.reference_title: Haploinsufficiency of A20.
evidence.snippet: arthralgia/arthritis (~34%), typically relapsing and/or remitting nonerosive inflammatory polyarthritis with synovitis, and rarely resembling rheumatoid arthritis or psoriatic-like erosions

nodes.description: Persistent canonical NF-kappa-B signalling in immune cells, demonstrated functionally in patient-derived mononuclear cells and in cell lines expressing the mutant protein.

evidence.reference_title: A novel missense mutation in TNFAIP3 causes haploinsufficiency of A20.
evidence.snippet: Functional studies were performed in A20(c.1804A > T, p.T602S) patient-derived peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and THP-1 cell lines by lentivirus mediating stable over-expression of A20 and A20(c.1804A > T, p.T602S) to analyze the activity of NF-κB signaling pathway.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in TNFAIP3 leading to A20 haploinsufficiency cause an early-onset autoinflammatory disease.
evidence.snippet: Patient-derived cells show increased degradation of IκBα and nuclear translocation of the NF-κB p65 subunit together with increased expression of NF-κB-mediated proinflammatory cytokines.

nodes.description: A20 terminates NF-kappa-B signalling by editing ubiquitin chains on upstream components. Its loss removes a brake rather than adding an accelerator, which is why the resulting phenotype is broad and variable rather than stereotyped.

biological_processes: negative regulation of canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction

evidence.reference_title: A20-mediated negative regulation of canonical NF-κB signaling pathway.
evidence.snippet: Therefore, to keep the inflammatory response in check, elaborate negative regulatory mechanisms operate to terminate NF-κB activation at multiple levels by de novo synthesis of NF-κB inhibitory proteins, and orchestration of protein ubiquitination and deubiquitination.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in TNFAIP3 leading to A20 haploinsufficiency cause an early-onset autoinflammatory disease.
evidence.snippet: A20 restricts NF-κB signals via its deubiquitinase activity.

nodes.description: Recurrent genital ulceration accompanying the oral ulcers, which together produce the Behcet-like presentation.

evidence.reference_title: Haploinsufficiency of A20.
evidence.snippet: recurrent painful oral/genital ulcers, typically during disease flares (>70% of persons)

nodes.description: A second regulatory arm. A20 negatively regulates the NLRP3 inflammasome, and losing it in mouse myeloid cells produces an erosive arthritis that does not depend on TNF receptor 1. Graded HYPOTHETICAL for this disease because the evidence is a myeloid-specific complete knockout in mice rather than heterozygous loss in humans.

animal_models.description: Demonstrates that losing A20 derepresses the NLRP3 inflammasome and produces spontaneous arthritis that does not require TNF receptor 1, which is the evidence for a second arm beyond NF-kappa-B.
animal_models.name: A20 myeloid-specific knockout mouse

biological_processes: negative regulation of NLRP3 inflammasome complex assembly

evidence.reference_title: Negative regulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome by A20 protects against arthritis.
evidence.snippet: Rheumatoid arthritis in A20(myel-KO) mice is not rescued by deletion of tumour necrosis factor receptor 1 (ref. 2).

nodes.description: A second-line option for patients not controlled by TNF blockade, which is a substantial group given the roughly forty per cent non-response rate. Anakinra is a recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist; canakinumab and rilonacept are biologics against IL-1 beta. Described as effective in many individuals, which is not a rate.

evidence.reference_title: Haploinsufficiency of A20.
evidence.snippet: The IL-1 receptor antagonist anakinra is considered relatively safe during pregnancy due to its extremely short half-life, although data are limited.

nodes.description: The other second-line option, and a small-molecule class unlike IL-1 blockade. Contraindicated in pregnancy, which matters in a disease presenting in childhood and continuing through reproductive life.

evidence.reference_title: Haploinsufficiency of A20.
evidence.snippet: JAK inhibitors are contraindicated during pregnancy.

nodes.description: Recurrent painful oral ulceration during flares, the commonest manifestation and usually the presenting one.

evidence.reference_title: Haploinsufficiency of A20.
evidence.snippet: recurrent painful oral/genital ulcers, typically during disease flares (>70% of persons)

nodes.description: One form of the heterogeneous skin involvement, which also includes folliculitis, vasculitic purpura, urticaria and lupus-like macular rashes.

evidence.reference_title: Haploinsufficiency of A20.
evidence.snippet: skin involvement (~40%), including pustular rashes, folliculitis, vasculitic purpura, urticaria, lupus-like macular rashes, and eczematoid dermatitis

nodes.description: Fever attacks of three to seven days, present in about half of patients. Their presence is one of the features that distinguishes this disease from Behcet disease, where recurrent fever is not characteristic.

evidence.reference_title: Haploinsufficiency of A20.
evidence.snippet: recurrent fevers (~50%), typically lasting for three to seven days that can rarely progress to a cytokine storm and/or hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis

nodes.description: The clinical disease, and unusually broad for a monogenic condition. Mucosal ulceration dominates, but the phenotype spans fever, skin, gut, joints, eye and liver, and includes autoimmune as well as autoinflammatory features in the same patient. That breadth follows from losing a general brake on NF-kappa-B rather than from a lesion in one effector pathway.

evidence.reference_title: Haploinsufficiency of A20.
evidence.snippet: Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20), a complex immune dysregulation disease, is characterized by recurrent systemic immune dysfunction (i.e., inflammation and/or immune deficiency).

evidence.reference_title: Haploinsufficiency of A20 caused by a novel nonsense variant or entire deletion of TNFAIP3 is clinically distinct from Behçet's disease.
evidence.snippet: We identified c.1434C>A:p.(Cys478*) in one family and a 236 kb deletion at 6q23.3 containing TNFAIP3 in another family.

evidence.reference_title: A novel missense mutation in TNFAIP3 causes haploinsufficiency of A20.
evidence.snippet: Herein, we reported a novel TNFAIP3 (c.1804A > T, p.T602S) variation, which has not been reported before.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion. A heterozygous loss-of-function variant in TNFAIP3 halves functional A20. Nonsense, missense and whole-gene deletion alleles have all been reported, including a 236 kb deletion at 6q23.3, which is consistent with true haploinsufficiency rather than a dominant negative effect.

evidence.reference_title: Haploinsufficiency of A20 caused by a novel nonsense variant or entire deletion of TNFAIP3 is clinically distinct from Behçet's disease.
evidence.snippet: We identified c.1434C>A:p.(Cys478*) in one family and a 236 kb deletion at 6q23.3 containing TNFAIP3 in another family.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in TNFAIP3 leading to A20 haploinsufficiency cause an early-onset autoinflammatory disease.
evidence.snippet: Herein we describe a new disease caused by high-penetrance heterozygous germline mutations in TNFAIP3, which encodes the NF-κB regulatory protein A20, in six unrelated families with early-onset systemic inflammation.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in TNFAIP3 leading to A20 haploinsufficiency cause an early-onset autoinflammatory disease.
evidence.snippet: Mutant, truncated A20 proteins are likely to act through haploinsufficiency because they do not exert a dominant-negative effect in overexpression experiments.

nodes.description: The most effective single class in the largest treatment series. In a Japanese national survey, molecular targeted drugs were given to 44.4% of patients and anti-TNF agents were effective in 59.5% of those treated. Note what that means: roughly forty per cent did not respond, so this is the best available option rather than a reliable one, and eleven patients failed to achieve control on their initial agent.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical characteristics and treatment strategies for A20 haploinsufficiency in Japan: a national epidemiological survey.
evidence.snippet: Seventy-two HA20 patients were identified in Japan. And, 54 patients from 37 unrelated families were analyzed in detail.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical characteristics and treatment strategies for A20 haploinsufficiency in Japan: a national epidemiological survey.
evidence.snippet: The severity of A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) varies, with no established clinical guidelines for treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Haploinsufficiency of A20.
evidence.snippet: Supportive treatment: TNF inhibitors, the most used medications, directly target abnormal NF-κB signaling.
